column1: #zone label(pasture_commons) start(1; 1) message(One 6x5 footprint carries two zones at once: a pen/pasture named Paddock and a meeting area named Commons. Apply with the cursor on the top-left tile; the (6x5) extent fills down and to the right.)
title: Overlapping pasture and meeting area
tags: zone, pasture, meeting area, overlap, starter
description: One tile footprint that is two zones at once. The token n{name=Paddock}m{name=Commons}(6x5) stacks a pen/pasture (n) and a meeting area (m) on the same 6x5 area
column2: each with its own name property
column3: then one shared (6x5) extent expands both from the anchor cell down and to the right. DFHack applies every zone type in the cell to the same tiles
column4: so grazing animals and idling dwarves share the space
column5: which saves surface room near the entrance. Add a type letter to stack more zones (for example a garbage dump d over a pond)
column6: and give each its own {name ...} block. This is also the corpus's first example of the compact (WxH) area-extent form: one anchor cell paints the whole rectangle instead of filling a grid of repeated tokens.
